subject: Tiered TTL & backup snapshot retention — DPA redlines
messages:
From: Olivia Zhang <olivia.z@fintegrate.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Desai <sdesai@fintegrate.com>
Date: 2028-06-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Questions on retention tiers & backups for DPA

Hi Mina —

Thanks for sending over the draft DPA earlier this week. Our legal team flagged a few questions around how Redwood defines retention windows across primary data, telemetry, and snapshots/backups. High level: we need to confirm (1) whether backups (encrypted snapshots) inherit the same TTLs as primary records, or if they are treated as "archive tier" with a longer TTL, and (2) if you can produce a deletion certificate for a specific customer when snapshots are purged.

Two things we want to avoid: long-lived backups that contain plaintext customer data in EU regions, and any ambiguity that prevents us from certifying deletion to auditors. Can you clarify the model and, if needed, propose redline language we can review?

Appreciate quick turnaround — Fintegrate is on a tight schedule for its audit next month.

Best,
Olivia
Director, Product Security
Fintegrate Inc.

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Questions on retention tiers & backups for DPA

Olivia —

Thanks for the note and the context. Short answers up front: (a) snapshots/backups are considered a separate "backup tier" and we treat them conservatively (longer TTL) by default, but we can commit to customer-specific snapshot retention and deletion certification for EU customers in the DPA; (b) we can provide a signed deletion certificate and a short audit trail for snapshot purges, subject to lawful hold exceptions.

I've attached a proposed set of redlines that introduces a tiered TTL model: primary customer records (TTL-A), short-term pseudonymized telemetry (TTL-B), and encrypted backups/snapshots (TTL-C). The attached spreadsheet maps examples and suggested default windows. Key proposals:
- TTL-A (primary): default 30 days after last customer activity; customer may request earlier erasure.
- TTL-B (telemetry/logs): default 180 days; stored pseudonymized for debugging and quality monitoring.
- TTL-C (backups & snapshots): default 365 days; backups are encrypted-at-rest with per-customer keys for EU customers on request, and can be purged earlier on certified request.

We recommend language that allows exceptions for legal/regulatory holds, and a clause that requires Redwood to issue a deletion certificate within 10 business days for snapshot purges (unless block by lawful hold).

Looping in Karthik and Priyom to confirm the operational feasibility and to add any controls we should reference (e.g., key rotation windows, restore-test retention).

Thanks — I can hop on a short call if helpful.

Mina
Senior Lead, Customer Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachments: DPA_redline_tiered_retention_v3.pdf, backup_snapshots_matrix.xlsx

On Thu, Jun 14, 2028 at 10:03 AM Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com> wrote:
> Olivia —
> 
> Thanks for the note and the context. Short answers up front: (a) snapshots/backups are considered a separate "backup tier"...

Mina — thanks for the quick turnaround and the redlines. A few follow-ups from legal:
1) The 365-day default for TTL-C is longer than our internal policy; would Redwood consider a 180-day maximum for encrypted backups for EU customers, provided you implement per-customer key separation?
2) For deletion certificates, we need explicit language describing the certificate contents: timestamp, scope (snapshot IDs / backup retention ranges), and the method (zeroing keys vs overwriting storage). Saying "purged" without method is insufficient for our auditors.
3) We also want to ensure that if a snapshot is retained for incident investigation, you document chain-of-custody and produce access logs for that snapshot upon request.

Happy to accept the tiered approach in principle — we just need narrower maximum windows and more prescriptive certificate language.

Regards,
Fintegrate Legal

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>

Date: 2028-06-14T15:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on retention tiers & backups for DPA

Legal team — appreciate the precision. Operational notes from Karthik/Priyom (copied):

- Per-customer key separation for EU customers: feasible. We can offer customer key separation for production snapshots in the Private and Dedicated deployments; hosted customers can opt into KMS-backed per-customer keys with an admin enablement step.
- Suggested compromise on TTL-C: default 365 days for hosted customers, with a guaranteed cap of 180 days for EU jurisdiction customers who request per-customer keying in writing (that becomes part of the subscription addendum).
- Deletion certificate contents: we will include (i) snapshot IDs / archive identifiers, (ii) timestamp of purge, (iii) method (cryptographic key destruction or data overwrite), and (iv) an auditor-facing change-log of who triggered the action. We can commit to producing that within 10 business days unless a lawful hold is in place.
- Chain-of-custody & access logs: we can provide an export of audit events for the snapshot (who accessed, when, and what operation) for a rolling 12-month window.

Proposed language change (high level) to the DPA: add a clause that allows customers to opt into an EU short-backup-policy (TTL-C = 180 days) conditioned on per-customer key separation; otherwise default TTL-C = 365 days. Also expand the deletion-certificate appendix with the fields above.

Priyom and Karthik, please flag any gotchas here. If this is acceptable, I'll produce a redline v4 with the prescriptive certificate format and the opt-in addendum language.

Thanks —
Mina

If you can drop in those two items in v4, we should be able to sign the DPA next week. Appreciate the flexibility on the EU cap.
